metaData.originalTitle: Who Does What? Team Topologies for the Agentic Platform
metaData.title: Who Does What? Team Topologies for the Agentic Platform
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article applies Team Topologies to the agentic platform, defining team types and interactions to distribute the transformed cognitive load of AI-driven production.
metaData.summary: The article extends Team Topologies (Skelton & Pais) to the context of AI agents producing applications. It argues that cognitive load in agentic production does not disappear but compresses onto a single person, becoming an "anticipation burden" and "cognitive throughput" problem. The agentic platform absorbs part of this burden by making itself queryable by agents. The author adapts the four team types: stream-aligned teams become non-technical business teams; the platform team provides systemic context, guardrails, and tooling as self-service; enabling teams temporarily bridge gaps; complicated subsystem teams handle deep AI infrastructure. Three interaction modes—facilitating, X-as-a-Service, collaboration—evolve as teams and platform mature. Governance (shadow IT prevention) and a graduation path (rule of three for guardrail systemization) are proposed to make the model sustainable. The article concludes that business teams can become stream-aligned without coding, as the platform absorbs technical complexity, while developers shift to building the platform.

mainPoints.point: Cognitive load in agentic production compresses from sequential roles to an anticipation burden on a single person.
mainPoints.explanation: Where human roles once spread complexity over time, agents produce instantly. The human must foresee all questions upfront, creating a throughput problem the platform must absorb.

mainPoints.point: Stream-aligned teams can be non-technical business teams because the platform absorbs operational and technical complexity.
mainPoints.explanation: The platform guarantees production reliability (deployment, monitoring, systemic guardrails). Business teams focus on intent and dynamic context, not end-to-end operations.

mainPoints.point: The platform matures when guardrails are automatic, deployments are self-service, and decision traceability exists.
mainPoints.explanation: Observable criteria include guardrail coverage, pipeline reliability, self-service share, documentation completeness, and audit trails. Without these, the platform cannot absorb operational responsibility.

mainPoints.point: A graduation path (rule of three) ensures guardrails move from team-specific to platform-owned.
mainPoints.explanation: When three teams reinvent the same guardrail, it becomes a candidate for systemization. The platform product owner generalizes and documents it, preventing local reinvention and scaling reliability.

mainPoints.point: Ease of production must be matched by ease of oversight to prevent shadow IT.
mainPoints.explanation: Centralized deployment, monitoring, and usage metrics give systemic visibility. The platform's product owner tracks active applications, flags those that fail security checks, and triggers deprecation.

keyQuotes: The agentic platform defines what needs to be provided. Team Topologies defines who provides it, and how teams interact to make it happen.
Cognitive load does not disappear with AI --- it transforms. It first becomes an anticipation burden: everything the human must foresee before launching the agent, or the output will fall short.
The developer does not disappear: they shift. They no longer produce the application --- they build the platform that enables others to produce it.

relatedArticles.title: ⚡️Satya Nadella: No Priors x Latent Space Crossover Special at Microsoft Build
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Satya Nadella outlines Microsoft's vision for an AI ecosystem platform where enterprises build their own frontier intelligence using multi-model harnesses, private evals, and rich context layers, redefining IP and business models.

relatedArticles.title: Codex Now Integrates Directly with Chrome on macOS and Windows
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI introduces a new Chrome extension for Codex on macOS and Windows, enabling the AI to operate directly within a user's live browser session to perform complex, parallel automation tasks using their active profile and direct code execution.

relatedArticles.title: Dario Amodei — Policy on the AI Exponential
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Dario Amodei argues that AI is advancing exponentially, creating a dangerous mismatch with slow-moving policy, and proposes concrete actions across regulation, economics, science, civil liberties, and geopolitics to meet the moment.

relatedArticles.title: Xiaomi MiMo， Explore and Love
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Xiaomi MiMo and TileRT achieve 1000+ tokens/s inference on a 1-trillion-parameter model using commodity GPUs through extreme model-system codesign, including FP4 quantization and DFlash speculative decoding.

relatedArticles.title: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5, a generally available Mythos-class model with state-of-the-art capabilities, alongside Claude Mythos 5 for trusted cybersecurity partners, with new safeguards to mitigate misuse risks.

relatedArticles.title: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI engineers detail a five-month experiment building a production software product with zero manually-written code, using Codex agents to achieve 10x velocity and redefining the engineer's role as system designer and feedback loop architect.

relatedArticles.title: Software Architecture Guide
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This page from Martin Fowler presents his perspective on software architecture, defining it as the important stuff in system design, and serves as a curated guide to his site's extensive resources on application and enterprise architecture.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing GPT-5.5
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI introduces GPT-5.5, a new category of AI that acts as an autonomous agent capable of planning, reasoning, and executing complex multi-step tasks across different applications.

relatedArticles.title: A harness for every task: dynamic workflows in Claude Code  | Claude
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Claude Code's dynamic workflows let Claude write custom agentic harnesses on the fly, enabling it to tackle complex, multi-step tasks that a single context window cannot handle reliably.

relatedArticles.title: Inside FAISS: Billion-Scale Similarity Search
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a deep, visual, and intuitive explanation of FAISS, covering the core ideas of IVF, Product Quantization, their combination in IVFPQ, and GPU acceleration, to enable billion-scale similarity search.
